::: {#exm-pairs-dfa}
#### A DFA for every a needing a b

@fig-pairs is the state diagram of the DFA (@def-dfa) $A = (S, \Sigma, \delta, q_0, F)$ with
$S = \set{q_0, q_1, q_2}$, $\Sigma = \set{\mathtt{a}, \mathtt{b}}$, $F = \set{q_0}$ and

$$
\ba
\delta(q_0, \mathtt{a}) &= q_1, & \delta(q_0, \mathtt{b}) &= q_0,
\\
\delta(q_1, \mathtt{a}) &= q_2, & \delta(q_1, \mathtt{b}) &= q_0,
\\
\delta(q_2, \mathtt{a}) &= q_2, & \delta(q_2, \mathtt{b}) &= q_2.
\ea
$$

Its states are the three things to remember in @sol-pairs:
$q_0$ for "every $\mathtt{a}$ so far has its $\mathtt{b}$",
$q_1$ for "the last symbol was an $\mathtt{a}$ still waiting",
and $q_2$ for "the check has failed".

::: {#fig-pairs}

![](../images/automata-pairs.png){fig-alt="Three circles in a row labeled q0, q1 and q2.
An arrow from the left, starting at no circle, points to q0, which is drawn as a double circle.
q0 has a loop labeled b.
An arrow labeled a goes from q0 to q1, and an arrow labeled b goes back from q1 to q0.
An arrow labeled a goes from q1 to q2, and q2 has a loop labeled a,b." width="70%"}

The DFA $A$, which checks that every $\mathtt{a}$ is followed by a $\mathtt{b}$.
